headline: We've explored more of the Moon's surface than the ocean floor
universal_truth: The unknown is closer than we think—mysteries exist in our own backyard
fun_facts: Less than 20% of the ocean floor has been mapped in detail; more people have walked on the Moon
The deepest point—Challenger Deep—is 36,000 feet down, deeper than Everest is tall
Life thrives at crushing depths, in total darkness, around volcanic vents at 700°F
discussion_questions: Why do you think we've explored space more than our own oceans?
What might we discover in the ocean depths that would change everything?
What unexplored depths exist in your own life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: We've sent humans to the Moon, robots to Mars, telescopes to the edge of the solar system. Yet right here on Earth, beneath the waves, lies a world we've barely glimpsed. The deep ocean is the last great frontier—and it's stranger than any alien planet.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: The deep ocean should be dead—no light, crushing pressure, near-freezing cold. Yet life thrives there, in ways that seem impossible. What could possibly survive in such conditions?
cliff.prompt: How does life survive in the deep ocean?

options.text: Life adapts to extreme conditions—using chemical energy instead of sunlight
options.response: Yes. Hydrothermal vents support entire ecosystems powered by chemicals, not the Sun.

options.text: Light from glowing organisms provides energy for food chains
options.response: Bioluminescence exists, but the energy source is more fundamental...

q1.title: The Unmapped World
q1.script: We've mapped only about 20% of the ocean floor in detail. The rest remains largely unknown—dark, unexplored, full of mysteries. More people have walked on the Moon than have visited the deepest trenches.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Unmapped World"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Crushing Depths
q2.script: At Challenger Deep, pressure is over 1,000 times surface pressure—enough to crush a submarine. Yet fish, shrimp, and microbes live there. Life finds a way into places that should be impossible.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Alien Oases
q3.script: In 1977, scientists discovered hydrothermal vents—underwater volcanoes hosting life independent of sunlight. Giant tube worms, blind shrimp, and strange bacteria thrive on chemical energy. It changed how we think about life's possibilities.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The greatest mysteries aren't always far away. The deep ocean reminds us that wonder exists in our own world, undiscovered. Before seeking the exotic elsewhere, explore the depths of what's already here.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 55. Tomorrow, we'll discover how rivers shape the land. Until then, remember: more than 80% of Earth's living space is unexplored. Mystery is close.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Inner Depths - Explore What's Close
growTrack.learning_objective: Discover unexplored depths in familiar territory
growTrack.activity: What's something close to you—a relationship, a place, a subject—that you've only explored on the surface? Commit to going deeper this week. Ask new questions, visit unexplored corners, read beyond the headlines. Depth rewards explorers.
